title: Fine-tune Gemma 3 with QLoRA (single GPU)
description: Fine-tune Google Gemma 3 12B with QLoRA (4-bit) on a single 16GB GPU using Soup CLI. Config, training, and GGUF export.

blocks.html:
Fine-tune Gemma 3 with QLoRA (single GPU)

QLoRA combines 4-bit base model quantization with LoRA adapters, which is the setup used to fit Gemma 3 12B on a single 16 GB GPU (RTX 4080, A4000). Soup publishes no measured peak for this config; soup profile --config gemma3.yaml --gpu rtx4080 prints an analytical estimate for your card.

Why QLoRA?

  • The frozen base weights take about a quarter of the memory of 16-bit weights
  • The QLoRA paper reports that it preserves 16-bit fine-tuning task performance on the tasks it measured; Soup has not measured that for Gemma 3
  • Works on consumer hardware

1. Install

Since v0.71.0 the base soup-cli package is a light, PyTorch-free CLI. [train] adds the training stack; [fast] adds Unsloth on top. Installing [fast] alone cannot train. Since v0.77.0 Soup needs Python 3.11 to 3.13 (>=3.11,<3.14); on Python 3.10, pip keeps installing v0.76.x.

2. Config

blocks.code:
base: google/gemma-3-12b-it
task: sft
backend: unsloth            # root-level, NOT under training

data:
  train: train.json
  format: alpaca
  max_length: 2048          # sequence length lives under data

training:
  quantization: 4bit        # the key is quantization, not quant
  epochs: 3
  lr: 2.0e-4                # the key is lr, not learning_rate
  batch_size: 1
  gradient_accumulation_steps: 16
  gradient_checkpointing: true   # since v0.77.0 the default false turns Unsloth's off
  lora:
    r: 16                   # LoRA turns on when r > 0; there is no enabled flag
    alpha: 16
    use_rslora: true
    target_modules: [q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj]

output: ./runs/gemma3

blocks.html:
Note the key flags:

  • quantization: 4bit — 4-bit NF4 quantization of base model (the key is quantization; quant is not a field, and since v0.75.0 it is refused as an unknown key; v0.74.0 only reported it). It applies to task: sft. On the tasks whose trainer never quantises the base (distill, classifier, reranker, cross_encoder, prm, moe_lora_routing, unlearn and asr) an explicit 4bit or 8bit (or load_in_8bit: true) is refused at load since v0.77.0: training.quantization: 4bit has no effect on task='reranker': its trainer never quantises the base, so no run can honour it. Delete the line or set quantization: none. Refused as of Soup v0.77. v0.76 loaded it with a warning and treated it as none (#795)
  • use_rslora: true — rank-stabilized LoRA (v0.21.0+), better for larger models. On backend: unsloth it is applied only since v0.77.0 (#1853, #1899): through v0.76.x the flag loaded and was never read there, so a run with this config trained plain-LoRA scaling (alpha / r) with nothing said. Results from such a run change on v0.77.0; drop the flag to keep the old behaviour
  • gradient_checkpointing: true — since v0.77.0 the Unsloth backend honours this key (#1981). Through v0.76.x it always used Unsloth's own checkpointing kernel; now the schema default false turns checkpointing off, so the config sets true to keep it
  • batch_size: 1 with gradient_accumulation_steps: 16 — effective batch of 16 on tight VRAM

Before you train

Run soup doctor --config gemma3.yaml first. Since v0.76.0 many more settings are refused when the config loads, each naming the field and what to change, so a config that loaded on an older release can stop loading. soup doctor --config prints the error and exits 2 without loading a model (it stops at the first cross-field refusal, so fix that setting and run it again until it prints no error), and since v0.77.0 it no longer prints All checks passed! above a refusal. Several things v0.76 only warned about are refused at v0.77.0, for example a staged field (validated, read by nothing) set away from its default, which stops the load with a line ending refused as of v0.77. Delete the line., and the deprecated data.remove_unused_columns: true. See Config refusals.

3. Train

In a script or CI job, pass --yes: since v0.77.0 soup train with its stdin piped or redirected and no --yes exits 3 instead of waiting at the confirmation prompt.

Monitor VRAM with nvidia-smi in another terminal. The peak depends on data.max_length and the batch size, and no peak is published here for this config; if it does not fit your card, see the out-of-memory note below.

4. Merge and export

blocks.code:
# Dequantize, merge LoRA, save a full fp16 model (the default --save-format)
soup merge --adapter ./runs/gemma3 --output ./gemma3-merged

# Or export directly to GGUF q4_k_m
soup export --model ./runs/gemma3 --format gguf --quant q4_k_m

blocks.html:
Common issues

OOM during backward pass? Reduce data.max_length to 1024, and check that gradient checkpointing is on (the config above sets it; since v0.77.0 leaving it out turns it off):

blocks.code:
training:
  loss_watchdog: true          # a bool, not a block
  loss_watchdog_threshold: 2.0 # spike factor vs the running mean (default 3.0)
  loss_watchdog_patience: 5
